what_this_is: The catalogue of Oracle PL/SQL constructs the converter recognises. Each is a row: a regex that detects it in source, the tier that handles it, what it becomes in PL/pgSQL, and -- for the rule tier -- a marker that must appear in the converted text (parity) and whether the Oracle form must be gone from it (residue). Adding a construct is adding a row. Tiers: rule = deterministic rewrite, no model; model = needs judgement, routed to the reasoning tier; manual = no PostgreSQL equivalent, a decision for a person.

constructs.name: NVL()
constructs.note: Identical two-argument null-coalescing semantics.

constructs.name: SYSDATE
constructs.note: Oracle DATE carries time to the second and no zone; LOCALTIMESTAMP alone carries microseconds, which would make equality comparisons against stored DATE values fail.

constructs.name: SYSTIMESTAMP
constructs.note: Both carry a time zone.

constructs.name: SELECT ... INTO
constructs.note: Oracle raises NO_DATA_FOUND on zero rows and TOO_MANY_ROWS on more than one. PL/pgSQL does that only with STRICT; without it the variable is silently set to NULL and every EXCEPTION handler written for Oracle becomes dead code.

constructs.name: :NEW / :OLD
constructs.note: Trigger row references drop the colon.

constructs.name: RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR()
constructs.note: Oracle's -20000..-20999 range has no SQLSTATE; the number is preserved in DETAIL so an application matching on it can be found.

constructs.name: DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE()
constructs.note: Diagnostic output; goes to the client's notice channel.

constructs.name: DUP_VAL_ON_INDEX
constructs.note: Same condition, different name.

constructs.name: COMMIT / ROLLBACK
constructs.note: A PostgreSQL procedure may commit only when CALLed outside a transaction block. A function never can; a function that commits is routed to the model tier.

constructs.name: %TYPE
constructs.note: Same syntax; resolved against the target's table at creation time, which is why the compile gate needs a shadow schema.

constructs.name: %ROWTYPE
constructs.note: Same syntax.

constructs.name: NO_DATA_FOUND
constructs.note: Same condition name; only raised by SELECT INTO STRICT.

constructs.name: TOO_MANY_ROWS
constructs.note: Same condition name.

constructs.name: WHEN OTHERS
constructs.note: Same syntax.

constructs.name: RETURNING ... INTO
constructs.note: Same syntax in PL/pgSQL.

constructs.name: Oracle scalar types
constructs.note: Mapped by convert/types.json. NUMBER(p,0) becomes the smallest exact integer type that holds p digits, the same optimisation AWS's accelerator applies to keys.

constructs.name: TYPE ... AS OBJECT
constructs.note: Attributes only. Methods, inheritance and quoted mixed-case names are manual.

constructs.name: VARRAY(n) OF
constructs.postgres: DOMAIN over an array with a cardinality CHECK
constructs.note: The element limit is kept as a CHECK constraint, so the target refuses what the source refused.

constructs.name: TABLE OF
constructs.note: Unbounded collection becomes an unbounded array.

constructs.name: PACKAGE (specification)
constructs.note: PostgreSQL has no packages. The specification creates nothing; its members are checked against what the body produced.

constructs.name: PACKAGE BODY
constructs.postgres: one function or procedure per member, named package$member
constructs.note: Members are flattened. Package-level variables, cursors and initialisation blocks are state PostgreSQL cannot hold and are routed to the model tier.

constructs.name: row-level trigger
constructs.postgres: trigger function RETURNS trigger + CREATE TRIGGER
constructs.note: PostgreSQL triggers call a function. A BEFORE trigger must RETURN NEW or the row change is silently cancelled -- the converter adds the return.

constructs.name: statement-level trigger
constructs.postgres: trigger function + CREATE TRIGGER ... FOR EACH STATEMENT
constructs.note: Returns NULL; no row to hand back.

constructs.name: DECODE()
constructs.note: Argument pairs need restructuring into WHEN clauses; DECODE treats NULL = NULL as a match, CASE does not.

constructs.name: NVL2()
constructs.postgres: CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN a ELSE b END
constructs.note: Needs the arguments split at the expression level.

constructs.name: ROWNUM
constructs.note: Restructures the query; where ROWNUM sits relative to ORDER BY changes the result.

constructs.name: CONNECT BY
constructs.note: Hierarchical query rewrite; LEVEL, PRIOR and SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH each need a hand.

constructs.name: BULK COLLECT
constructs.note: Collection types differ; usually the loop that consumed it should become a single statement.

constructs.name: FORALL
constructs.note: Bulk DML has no direct form; the intent is a single INSERT ... SELECT or UPDATE ... FROM.

constructs.name: CURSOR ... IS
constructs.note: Supported, but declaration order and OPEN/FETCH forms differ.

constructs.name: REF CURSOR
constructs.note: Calling conventions differ; the consumer usually needs changing too.

constructs.name: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
constructs.note: Bind syntax differs; dynamic SQL is reviewed by a person regardless.

constructs.name: TO_CHAR()
constructs.postgres: to_char() with a PostgreSQL format model
constructs.note: Format models overlap but are not identical; a numeric TO_CHAR without a format is a cast.

constructs.name: TO_DATE()
constructs.note: Format models differ; the result type is timestamp, not date.

constructs.name: TRUNC()
constructs.note: Depends on the argument type, which the text alone does not carry.

constructs.name: INSTR()
constructs.note: Three- and four-argument forms have no direct equivalent.

constructs.name: LISTAGG()
constructs.note: WITHIN GROUP ordering moves inside the aggregate.

constructs.name: REGEXP_*()
constructs.note: Similar names, different argument orders and flags.

constructs.name: SQLCODE
constructs.note: Numeric codes become five-character states; any comparison against a number needs rewriting.

constructs.name: MERGE INTO
constructs.note: Depends on the target version.

constructs.name: PIPELINED
constructs.note: Table functions exist; the declaration shape differs.

constructs.name: INDEX BY
constructs.postgres: hstore, jsonb or a temp table
constructs.note: Associative arrays have no native equivalent.

constructs.name: SAVEPOINT
constructs.note: PL/pgSQL has no SAVEPOINT statement; a nested block is the idiom.

constructs.name: DBMS_* package
constructs.note: Each package is its own conversation.

constructs.name: UTL_* package
constructs.note: UTL_FILE, UTL_HTTP and friends need an extension or an application change.

constructs.name: definer-rights execution (AUTHID DEFINER, Oracle's default)
constructs.postgres: not added: SECURITY INVOKER is the PostgreSQL default
constructs.note: Recorded as not_translated on every routine, explicit or implicit. Adding SECURITY DEFINER widens privileges on the target and is a person's decision.

constructs.name: PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION
constructs.postgres: none native (dblink loopback is the workaround)
constructs.note: A decision about audit semantics, not a rewrite.

constructs.name: XML-schema generated type
constructs.postgres: none; the xml type has no schema-registered object types
constructs.note: Generated by XML schema registration on the source. The application's XML handling is the real question.

constructs.name: ROWID / UROWID
constructs.note: Any logic keyed on ROWID needs a real key.

constructs.name: database link
constructs.note: A network path and a credential decision.

constructs.name: LANGUAGE JAVA
constructs.note: Java stored procedures are rewritten by a person.

constructs.name: Advanced Queuing
constructs.note: Queues are out of scope for this tool.

constructs.name: TYPE BODY
constructs.note: Method dispatch has no equivalent; the calling code decides the shape.

constructs.name: MEMBER / MAP / ORDER / CONSTRUCTOR
constructs.note: Same as TYPE BODY.

constructs.name: NOT FINAL (type inheritance)
constructs.postgres: none; composite types do not inherit
constructs.note: A modelling decision.

constructs.name: quoted mixed-case identifier
constructs.note: PostgreSQL folds unquoted names to lower case, Oracle to upper. A quoted mixed-case name must be quoted everywhere it is used, including in application code.

constructs.name: GOTO
constructs.note: Restructure the control flow.
